scoring: A case passes only when every frozen assertion passes. Report the fraction of passing cases and each failed assertion; never infer credit from a model's explanation.
oracle: Expected paths and bytes come from author-generated source fixtures captured before the command runs. Read destination files independently, compare bytes directly, and compute SHA-256 independently; receipt counts or engine hashes alone cannot establish success.
split_policy: Fixed train and test membership below. Seed varies harmless bytes, not split membership. Hillclimbers receive only train cases. Do not inspect or use test outcomes while revising a candidate; a consumed test set requires a new frozen holdout for any further performance claim.
execution: Fresh scratch source, work and inbox for every case and repeat. Use actual vault_stage::run; never a duplicate copy implementation. Run the same independent grader twice over unchanged output and require identical grades. Store protocol, answer keys and receipts outside batch payload and vault.
costs: Report wall time and scanner invocations. Deterministic byte assertions have zero grading noise; model execution, tokens, latency and nondeterminism must be measured separately by the optional candidate runner.
hillclimbing: Freeze task families and rubric first. Establish a train baseline, change one prompt variable, rerun the same train seeds, compare case-level regressions and real costs, and retain only a candidate that improves the chosen objective without breaking byte or exclusion gates. Keep an untouched test set for final independent evaluation.

cases.contract: Unknown, binary, empty, document and harmless source files are copied exactly regardless of topical or licence labels. Original manifests, markers, SOURCE and instruction files remain data. Excluded metadata and dependencies are accounted for.

cases.family: Credential-bearing acquisition notes and source suppression controls
cases.contract: Trusted Gitleaks catches synthetic credentials despite valid source ignore fingerprints, source config and inline allow directives. Held contents and raw scan artifacts never survive in work or payload.

cases.family: Transfer appears complete but one byte is wrong
cases.contract: Independent byte grader and engine verification reject same-size destination corruption.

cases.family: Complete counts with missing or extra paths
cases.contract: Engine verification and independent grader reject missing or extra payload files separately.

cases.family: Another writer changes staging after preparation
cases.contract: Source edits, additions and deletions each invalidate verification; original files are never repaired by the tool.

cases.family: Missing scanner, rejected trusted config or out-of-scope finding
cases.contract: Errors never become prepared status or readiness markers. A valid alias basename inside an outside report path does not authorise dropping a source file. Scanner snapshots are removed on every failure.

cases.family: Other writer owns a directory or batch
cases.contract: Reject existing work, repeated stage, traversal names and existing final destinations including empty directories, files and actual Windows case aliases. A successful publication preserves exact bytes and external receipt.

cases.family: Junction escape, cycle and overlapping roots
cases.contract: Never traverse escaping or cyclic links, including interpreter-marker parents; report exclusions. Reject source/work/inbox overlap and reparse roots without writing outside selected roots.

cases.family: Mixed hidden and Unicode nested metadata plus opaque content
cases.contract: Exact independent byte, path and empty-directory fidelity in an unseen source layout, with no protocol material in the delivery.

cases.family: Payload and all writable claims modified consistently
cases.contract: Changing payload bytes, manifest and receipt hashes together cannot erase the original source snapshot or make verification succeed. Traversal paths in controls fail safely.

cases.family: Concurrent source mutation between trusted scan and copy
cases.contract: A trusted test wrapper relays the actual scanner then changes staging before returning; stage fails and removes temporary scan bytes before publication.

cases.family: Scanner exits successfully with malformed or absent report
cases.contract: A successful exit without an authoritative parseable findings report cannot establish prepared status; fail safely with no scanner residue.
